inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes production deploys and migrations on request and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can access the assistant
Cloud audit log records production actions
Chat transcript stores the request context
Separate tamper-resistant agent action provenance bound to each production action

findings.title: Missing attributable agent action provenance for production actions executed under the engineer's identity

forecast.watch_signal: No change-triggered control decay identified because the required provenance control is absent already; reassess if unattended scope expands or logging design changes.

evidence.observation: Production actions are recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name because the agent uses the engineer's personal access token.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript.
Engineers can delete their own chat history, so the request-to-action linkage is not tamper resistant.
The agent is instructed to deploy or run migrations when asked and not to ask for confirmation, increasing reliance on post hoc attribution rather than pre-action verification.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, so an unattributable action can have severe operational consequence.

recommendations.action: Bind every agent-initiated production action to tamper-resistant provenance that records the authenticated requester, the exact prompt or approved intent, the agent identity, and the executed action in a non-deletable record separate from user-editable chat history.
Log agent actions under a distinct agent principal or append immutable agent attribution fields to cloud audit entries so reviewers can distinguish engineer actions from delegated agent actions.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts say only that engineers use SSO to reach the assistant; they do not say how the assistant process identity itself is authenticated to surrounding systems.
The provided design does not describe config integrity, prompt change control, or deployment hardening for the agent process.
No egress capability or external recipient is described in the reviewed design, so this process has no declared disclosure path across a trust boundary.
The design exposes only single production actions and does not describe loops, spawning, spend, or unattended execution horizons that would support a present denial-of-service property finding.
The agent acts using the requesting engineer's delegated personal token rather than a broader shared or service credential, so no broader authority than the user is declared.
The artifacts do not describe access controls, retention, or tenant separation for chat transcripts, so disclosure exposure of this store cannot be assessed.
No availability dependency or quota on chat history is described as necessary for safe operation of the reviewed deploy functions.
The case says actions are recorded in the cloud audit log but does not describe whether log integrity is immutable or protected against privileged modification.
The design does not state who can read cloud audit logs or whether they contain sensitive payload details.
No evidence shows the audit log is a runtime dependency whose unavailability would block or amplify the production actions in scope.
The artifacts do not describe message integrity or transport protections for the engineer-to-agent chat channel.
The artifacts do not describe whether the chat channel is encrypted end to end or what intermediaries can read its contents.
This flow is internal and does not cross a trust boundary, so STRIDE coverage for data flows does not apply here in this schema.
The design does not say whether the deploy request passed from agent to deployment system has integrity protection or independently recorded parameters.
The deployment action flow is internal and no cross-boundary disclosure channel is declared for this path.
This flow is internal and does not cross a trust boundary, so STRIDE coverage for data flows does not apply here in this schema.
The artifacts do not describe integrity controls on the migration command or how its exact parameters are preserved for later review.
The migration action flow is internal and no external disclosure sink is described in the reviewed artifacts.
This flow is internal and does not cross a trust boundary, so STRIDE coverage for data flows does not apply here in this schema.

rating.rationale: Present risk is driven by a repudiation property failure: production actions are executed under the engineer's own token, cloud audit entries therefore attribute actions to the human rather than distinctly to the agent, and the only intent record is deletable chat history. No declared control restores attributable, tamper-resistant action provenance. Missing artifacts include source code, deployment configuration, and audit-log integrity settings; these gaps limit assessment of spoofing, tampering, and transport protections, but they do not change the repudiation finding evidenced by the runtime notes.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, infrastructure-as-code, or detailed runtime configuration was provided, so identity binding, transport integrity, and log immutability could not be verified.
No explicit tool manifest or API contract was provided; capability details were inferred from the stable ids and runtime notes.
